- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.20), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match downward pressure.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — cap forecast rise to 5-7% above recent peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-forecasting in early 30d window when prices are trending up, under-forecasting when trending down — adjust for recent 7-day momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive swings (e.g., 0.06–0.11) with no clear direction, model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of true price, especially in 30d horizon.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model is likely underestimating long-term trend — increase forecast by 2–3% for next 7-day window.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.10–0.20), model often fails to capture short-term reversals — use sentiment average over 3-day window to smooth and adjust forecast direction.
